name: Ageing
blurb: Dân số già, hưu trí, chăm sóc

words.definitionEn: the process of growing older, especially in relation to individuals or populations
words.example: Population ageing is placing considerable pressure on public healthcare systems.

words.definitionEn: relating to the characteristics of a population
words.example: Demographic changes are transforming the structure of many developed societies.

words.definitionEn: the length or duration of a person’s life
words.example: Improved medical treatment has contributed significantly to human longevity.

words.definitionEn: the ability or tendency of a population to produce children
words.example: Declining fertility has accelerated the ageing of the national population.

words.definitionEn: the state of relying on others for financial or physical support
words.example: A rising old-age dependency ratio may place a heavier burden on workers.

words.definitionEn: a regular payment made to a retired person
words.example: Many citizens rely on a state pension after leaving the workforce.

words.definitionEn: the period when a person stops working permanently
words.example: Retirement policies should reflect the increasing life expectancy of the population.

words.definitionEn: all the people who are available for work in a society or organisation
words.example: An ageing workforce may require employers to redesign working conditions.

words.definitionEn: the skills and qualities that make someone suitable for employment
words.example: Lifelong training can improve the employability of older workers.

words.definitionEn: unfair treatment based on characteristics such as age
words.example: Age discrimination can prevent experienced employees from remaining in work.

words.definitionEn: a person who provides regular care for someone who is ill or dependent
words.example: Family caregivers often experience considerable emotional and financial stress.

words.definitionEn: relating to the health and care of older people
words.example: Governments need to expand geriatric services in regional hospitals.

words.definitionEn: a condition of physical weakness commonly associated with old age
words.example: Early intervention can reduce frailty among vulnerable older adults.

words.definitionEn: a condition involving a decline in memory and other mental abilities
words.example: Specialist services are essential for families affected by dementia.

words.definitionEn: continuing for a long time and often difficult to cure
words.example: Older adults are more likely to suffer from chronic health conditions.

words.definitionEn: the condition of being diseased or the rate of disease in a population
words.example: Public health programmes can lower morbidity among elderly citizens.

words.definitionEn: the number or rate of deaths in a population
words.example: Improved prevention has reduced mortality from several age-related diseases.

words.meaningVi: dịch vụ chăm sóc sức khỏe
words.definitionEn: the organised provision of medical services
words.example: An ageing society requires greater investment in accessible healthcare.

words.meaningVi: việc đưa vào cơ sở chăm sóc
words.definitionEn: the process of placing a person in a residential institution for long-term care
words.example: Institutionalisation should not be the default solution for elderly people living alone.

words.definitionEn: involving or affecting different generations
words.example: Intergenerational programmes can strengthen mutual understanding within communities.

words.definitionEn: a lack of contact and interaction with other people
words.example: Social isolation can seriously damage the mental health of retired individuals.

words.definitionEn: the degree to which services or places can be used by people with different needs
words.example: Improving accessibility is necessary if older residents are to use public transport independently.

words.definitionEn: a place designed or provided for people to live in
words.example: Affordable accommodation can help older people remain in their communities.

words.definitionEn: treatment intended to restore a person’s health or abilities
words.example: Post-operative rehabilitation enables many elderly patients to regain independence.

words.definitionEn: action taken to stop a disease or problem from occurring
words.example: Disease prevention is generally more cost-effective than long-term treatment.

words.definitionEn: the ability to make one’s own decisions and live independently
words.example: Care policies should protect the autonomy of older patients.

words.definitionEn: the sense of value and respect that every person deserves
words.example: Residential facilities must ensure that residents are treated with dignity.

words.definitionEn: the care and support provided to elderly people
words.example: The demand for professional eldercare is likely to grow substantially.

words.definitionEn: having more work or responsibility than can reasonably be managed
words.example: Overburdened families may be unable to provide adequate care for elderly relatives.

words.definitionEn: the ability of a system to continue effectively over time
words.example: The sustainability of public pension systems depends on careful economic planning.

words.definitionEn: the act of supplying a service or facility
words.example: The provision of community-based care can reduce pressure on hospitals.

words.definitionEn: a benefit or payment that a person has a legal right to receive
words.example: Pension entitlement should be transparent and accessible to all eligible citizens.

words.definitionEn: a fixed amount of money paid regularly, usually after retirement
words.example: Some retirees purchase an annuity to secure a stable income for life.

words.definitionEn: involving regular payments made by an individual or employer
words.example: A contributory pension scheme can provide workers with greater financial security.

words.definitionEn: provided only after assessing a person’s income and financial resources
words.example: Means-tested benefits can direct limited public funds towards the poorest pensioners.

words.definitionEn: not provided through a formal organisation or professional service
words.example: Informal care supplied by relatives remains vital in many ageing societies.

words.definitionEn: involving several generations of a family or community
words.example: Multigenerational households can offer older adults companionship and practical support.

words.definitionEn: unfair prejudice or discrimination against people because of their age
words.example: Ageism in recruitment deprives businesses of valuable experience.

words.definitionEn: the length of time that a person or organism is expected to live
words.example: A longer lifespan does not necessarily guarantee a better quality of life.

words.definitionEn: a person who receives a pension, especially after retirement
words.example: Many pensioners struggle to meet living costs when prices rise sharply.

words.definitionEn: involving much sitting and little physical activity
words.example: A sedentary lifestyle can increase the risk of chronic disease in later life.

words.definitionEn: relating to mental processes such as thinking and remembering
words.example: Regular mental activity may help older adults maintain cognitive function.

words.definitionEn: intended to relieve suffering rather than cure an illness
words.example: Palliative services should be available to patients with advanced conditions.

words.definitionEn: a short period of relief from a difficult responsibility or situation
words.example: Respite services give family caregivers time to recover from prolonged stress.

words.definitionEn: the legal responsibility for caring for someone who cannot manage independently
words.example: Guardianship arrangements should respect the preferences of older people whenever possible.

words.definitionEn: the scientific study of ageing and the problems of older people
words.example: Gerontology can inform policies designed to support healthy ageing.

words.meaningVi: năng động, tích cực tham gia
words.definitionEn: involved in physical, social, or economic activities
words.example: Active ageing enables older citizens to contribute to their communities for longer.

words.definitionEn: able to produce useful results or make a valuable contribution
words.example: Older employees can remain productive when workplaces offer flexible arrangements.

words.meaningVi: thân thiện với người cao tuổi
words.definitionEn: designed to meet the needs and abilities of older people
words.example: Age-friendly cities provide safe transport, accessible housing, and inclusive public spaces.

words.definitionEn: a retirement savings system funded during a person’s working life
words.example: Compulsory superannuation can reduce dependence on government pensions.
